email.subject1: a signal play for dbt Labs
email.body1:
Ryan, saw dbt Labs closed the Fivetran merger and shipped dbt Copilot into AI-assisted data ops.

That kind of expansion usually means more majors accounts in play than the team can cover before territories settle, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for dbt Labs off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Ryan, quick follow-up for dbt Labs.

Post-merger, the majors number tends to climb faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say precisely how many meetings they need to book to hit it, so the coverage gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a recovery effort.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings dbt Labs needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Ryan, last bit of proof for dbt Labs.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to 2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged.

I pulled a benchmark of how dbt Labs' reply rate likely compares to peers. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Ryan, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling majors pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority while the merger settles, no problem at all. The integration stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your majors motion? I will tailor it to dbt Labs either way.
